candidates.title: ACSeL: Adaptive Configuration Search for Hardware-Constrained LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: Serving large language models (LLMs) under tight memory and latency service-level objectives (SLOs), including on edge devices, requires jointly selecting the model size, batch size, quantization algorithm, and mixed-precision quantization recipes. Exhaustive search over this combinatorially large space is infeasible. Unlike data-center serving, which often prioritizes throughput or generation speed, resource-constrained deployments typically set memory and latency budgets as constraints and then seek the configuration with the highest generation quality among feasible ones. To this end, we propose ACSeL, a framework that identifies configurations predicted to satisfy deployment constraints while achieving high predicted generation quality. To enable efficient quality estimation, we use Relative Model Quality Degradation (RMQD), a proxy based on the divergence between the candidate and reference models' next-token distributions over a small calibration corpus. Across the evaluated model sizes and precisions, RMQD is inexpensive to evaluate and strongly correlated with downstream benchmark performance. ACSeL combines (i) a lightweight quality surrogate that predicts RMQD directly from a configuration; (ii) Few-shot Median Calibration (FMC), which calibrates operator-profile-based latency estimates using a small number of end-to-end profiles; and (iii) a structured search algorithm BandPareto for exploring layerwise mixed-precision configurations. Experiments on an NVIDIA RTX A6000 workstation and an NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge platform show that FMC substantially improves deployment feasibility, while BandPareto + FMC achieves the highest feasibility and the lowest RMQD gaps to the best measured configurations in the evaluation set.

candidates.title: Affinity Engineering of a Hyaluronic Acid-Specific Carbohydrate-Binding Module Using a Rule-Constrained Large Language Model Agent
candidates.abstract: Abstract Hyaluronic acid (HA) is widely used in food and nutritional supplements, yet reliable quantification in complex matrices remains limited by the lack of cost-effective, high-affinity recognition elements. Carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) are stable, recombinantly accessible, and intrinsically selective for polysaccharides. However, their native affinity is often insufficient for sensitive analysis. Here, we developed a rule-constrained large language model (LLM)-based agent for affinity optimization of the HA-binding CBM SrCBM70. The agent converts structural, energetic, and evolutionary information into rule constraints that compress the mutation search space, then refines design through iterative feedback from experimental affinity data. After two rounds of iterative optimization, the double mutant E29W/T112S reached a Kd of 154 ± 7 nM, a 20.9-fold improvement over WT SrCBM70, and retained HA specificity. Mechanistic analysis suggested that E29W enhanced CH−π interactions and T112S expanded the protein–HA contact interface. This work provides a nanomolar HA-recognition element for food analysis and establishes an agentic protein engineering strategy with potential extension to CBM affinity engineering.

candidates.title: DreamRealm: Exploring and Materializing Hallucination Worlds for Trustworthy Vision-Language Models
candidates.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remain prone to visual hallucinations when correct responses depend on subtle visual details. One line of post-training methods constructs visual contrasts through image retrieval, generation, or editing to improve fine-grained perception. However, these contrasts are not built around the model's own hallucinations, making it difficult to ensure that supervision targets its actual perceptual confusions. Another line suppresses hallucinated outputs through response correction or preference learning under fixed image conditions, but leaves the design of supervision signals on the image-input side underexplored. Inspired by how humans correct misconceptions, we introduce DreamRealm, a post-training framework that explores diverse latent hallucinated responses, minimally edits original images to make them valid, and trains the model to assign each response to its supporting image. Our data construction pipeline, RealmForgePipe, mines observed and latent hallucinations from a target model and materializes them through image editing. Using hallucinations mined from Qwen3.5-9B, we construct the Realized Hallucination Dataset (RealmSet). Our training objective, RealmMatch, constructs a likelihood score matrix across image--response combinations and combines supervised learning with bidirectional contrastive losses to reinforce correct matches and suppress mismatches. Compared with the original Qwen3.5-9B model, DreamRealm improves performance across six visual perception and hallucination benchmarks, including gains of 7.26 percentage points in HallusionBench accuracy and 11.34 percentage points in MMVP pair accuracy. Together with ablation studies on data construction and training methods, these results demonstrate that hallucination assignment is a promising paradigm for improving visual perception and mitigating hallucinations.

candidates.title: A Kannada centric retrieval augmented generation system for Karnataka heritage knowledge access
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models produce fluent text, but in domain-specific and low-resource language settings they are prone to hallucination, weak factual grounding and limited multilingual coverage. These problems are acute for Kannada heritage information, where historical sources are fragmented, sparsely digitised and often available only as scanned documents. The presented work is on Retrieval Augmented Generation system for Kannada question answering over Karnataka cultural heritage documents. The system combines hybrid document ingestion using PyMuPDF and Tesseract OCR with per-page provenance, Kannada-aware Unicode normalisation, recursive chunking on a Kannada-aware separator hierarchy, a general-purpose multilingual sentence encoder, and exact cosine retrieval over a FAISS index. A deterministic passage selection rule combining an absolute and a relative similarity floor sets the number of retrieved passages from the score distribution, and the system abstains when no passage clears the absolute floor. Retrieved passages are supplied to locally deployed LLMs through FastAPI and Ollama with an instruction to answer only from them, enabling fully offline operation, each response lists the source page of every passage supplied to the model. The system was evaluated on 25 Kannada questions written by the research team (8 factual, 9 interpretive and 8 analytical) over a single 62-page heritage document. On this set, gemma3:4b obtained the highest scores on all four response-quality metrics and the lowest mean latency (3.97 s), with BERT-F1 of 0.850, 0.863 and 0.851 across the three tiers (0.855 aggregate). Across all models, BERT-F1 remained high and nearly flat across tiers, while ROUGE and alignment scores fell sharply on interpretive and analytical questions. We analyse this divergence and argue that, in a morphologically rich low-resource language, neither family of metrics is self-validating without retrieval-level and human evaluation. All reported tables are derived from a single per-question record log with automated consistency checks. The system offers a starting point for offline Kannada heritage question answering whose retrieval and grounding remain to be validated.

candidates.title: Large language model developments
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are generative artificial intelligence (AI) models trained with vast amounts of data and context, and excel at processing, understanding and generating human language, using transformer models to learn statistical relationships between tokens. LLMs are a subset of transformer models, and hence are closely related but not interchangeable. Given the ‘explosion’ of LLM research, the challenge is tracking emerging developments and matching LLMs to applications. This paper reviews LLM developments with the aim of understanding the underlying models’ computational strengths and weaknesses, building on previous work focusing on LLM optimization (Sharkey & Treleaven 2025 Optimising large language models: taxonomy and techniques. SSRN Scholarly Paper no. 5278456. Rochester, NY: SSRN). We find that despite their power, LLMs (transformers) face several key challenges. These include: (i) computational complexity and resource requirements—training and deploying large models is extremely costly and slow, and energy consumption is a concern; (ii) understanding long sequences and dependencies—even with enhancements, models can struggle with very long-range dependencies or context lengths beyond their window (e.g. maintaining coherence in a long document), which reflects the more fundamental absence of continual learning; (iii) interpretability and bias—it remains difficult to interpret why a model produces a given output, and models can inadvertently amplify biases present in training data; and (iv) optimization challenges, including fine-tuning for specific tasks without overfitting or losing generality and ensuring efficient inference (latency, the delay before a response is completed) for real-time applications. In summary, this review focuses on architectural, optimization and interpretability developments in LLMs. It does not aim to provide a systematic benchmark comparison, exhaustive implementation details or empirical performance evaluation, which are covered extensively elsewhere. The authors are committed to updating this review aligned to constant changes in the technology; please reach out with any additions.

candidates.title: Governed Retrieval Augmented Generation with Guardrails Role Based Access Control and Audit Logging
candidates.abstract: Enterprise retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) must preserve source permissions while controlling unsafe content and retaining audit evidence. This paper integrates permission-tagged ingestion, authorization-aware retrieval, guardrails, and correlated logging, and evaluates the authorization boundary in a reproducible synthetic diagnostic. Five retrieval strategies were compared across eight corpus randomizations, each containing 750 documents, 12 principals, and 360 queries under five policy conditions. SQLite FTS5 supplied exact lexical ranking; no language model or Amazon Bedrock deployment was evaluated. Indexed filtering alone admitted unauthorized context in an average 99.5% of role-revocation queries and 57.7% of document-revocation queries. Adding a current-permission recheck produced zero observed context violations in the tested conditions. With 10% of private index metadata removed, authorized recall was 92.1%; policy-service outages forced all protected methods to abstain. An independent recomputation verified the saved retrieval and policy decisions. These results illustrate a known stale-permission failure mode and its mitigation under a trusted policy model. They do not establish production security, generated-answer safety, or regulatory compliance.

candidates.title: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining
candidates.abstract: The full-attention layers of large language models (LLMs) make every generated token more expensive than the previous one, slowing models down on long-context tasks. Hybrid models reduce this cost by replacing most full-attention layers with linear-attention layers, but the first still dominate decoding at long contexts. We accelerate these remaining layers without any training or weight changes using combined sparse attention: each layer attends to a sliding window of recent tokens, a pinned prefix, and a fixed budget of most relevant tokens in the context. The window size and budget are found on a per-layer basis using a multi-objective search algorithm. Across six hybrid models from three families, from 4B to 397B parameters, the selected configurations preserve their baseline model's accuracy on 21 long-context datasets. Decoding 64k/256k tokens becomes up to 1.26x/2.22x faster on Qwen3.5-4B, 1.20x/2.23x on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 1.16x/2.06x on Ornith-1.0-397B.

candidates.title: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Personalized Reasoning of Vision-Language Models
candidates.abstract: People often make decisions by holistically reasoning over heterogeneous forms of personal information. In this paper, we study the relatively underexplored capability of multimodal personalized reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). To this end, we introduce \texttt{MPRBench}, a novel and comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate personalized reasoning across a wide range of tasks and real-world challenges. \texttt{MPRBench} consists of 12 sub-tasks and additionally supports interpretable analysis of representative error cases. Through extensive experiments, we find that current personalized MLLMs still struggle with personalized reasoning due to several key challenges, including inaccurate recognition of personalized concepts and sensitivity to irrelevant personal information. We hope that MPRBench will stimulate further research on personalized reasoning in MLLMs. Code and data are available at https://github.com/kkdh15/MPRBench

candidates.title: Weaver: Weaving Preference Evidence through Incremental Reasoning for Personalized Retrieval-Augmented Generation
candidates.abstract: Personalized retrieval-augmented generation requires extracting and applying user preferences from extended interaction histories. This task is challenging because preference evidence is scattered across past conversations and remains bound to specific temporal and situational contexts. Consequently, isolated fragments rarely provide complete support for a response, while preferences expressed under different conditions are easily conflated. To address these limitations, we propose Weaver, a framework that incrementally weaves memory-conditioned retrieval trajectories with compositional preference reasoning for personalized responses. Weaver operates on a Dual-Layer Retrieval and Reasoning Graph that couples an upper Intent Dependency Graph with a lower Memory-Conditioned Retrieval Trajectory Graph. Dependency Information Gap Tracking represents the information needed to answer the current request and its prerequisite dependencies in the upper graph. Memory-Conditioned Incremental Retrieval uses established premises and clues from retrieved conversations to locate missing evidence, recording the resulting retrieval trajectories in the lower graph. Scope-Aware Compositional Reasoning jointly interprets the accumulated evidence to determine which preferences apply to the request. It identifies complementary and alternative support and distinguishes conflicting claims within the same temporal and situational context. These conclusions iteratively update task premises and remaining information gaps, guiding subsequent retrieval to establish a coherent contextual basis for the final response. Experiments on personalized RAG benchmarks, particularly PersonaMem, demonstrate that Weaver outperforms leading baselines in both evidence completeness and answer quality.

candidates.title: Quantized large language models in biomedical natural language processing: evaluation and recommendation
candidates.abstract: Large language models have demonstrated strong capabilities in biomedical natural language processing, yet their rapid growth in size and computational requirements creates a barrier to local deployment in privacy-sensitive settings. In this study, we evaluated the impact of quantization on 12 general-purpose and biomedical large language models across eight benchmark datasets covering named entity recognition, relation extraction, multi-label classification, and question answering. Using Transformers with BitsAndBytes, we found that 4-bit and 8-bit weight quantization substantially reduced peak GPU memory while often preserving task performance, although latency generally increased and degradation was task- and model-dependent. We further evaluated deployment-oriented AWQ, GPTQ, and FP8 checkpoints with vLLM on representative biomedical tasks and model scales. We also quantified invalid-output rates, prompt overhead, and few-shot memory effects. These results provide a systematic benchmark of quantization trade-offs for biomedical NLP and show that weight-memory reduction can make otherwise difficult-to-host large models feasible for local deployment on GPUs with sufficient VRAM, including high-memory consumer GPUs.

candidates.title: Problem-Conditioned Interface Fusion: A Modular Language Model Framework for Multi-Objective Branch-Specific Post-Training
candidates.abstract: Multi-objective post-training may cause interference in shared parameters, yet assigning objectives to private branches does not ensure that their outputs can be combined directly. We propose problem-conditioned interface fusion: after joint pretraining and partitioned specialization, the backbone and experts are frozen, while a fusion layer learns candidate selection, low-rank input adaptation, branch-message reading, and bounded residual synthesis. The framework maintains a single main hidden-state stream and uses predictions of branch contributions and complementarity as auxiliary learning objectives. We derive local correction bounds, zero-message response, permutation invariance for the same candidate set, and pure-path preservation under explicit cache conditions. We also discuss cross-layer perturbation propagation under additional smoothness assumptions. A potential conflict between reasoning and literary expression serves as a motivating example, not an established universal causal relationship. No model training or capability validation has been conducted; the proposed benefits, learnability, and extension behavior remain hypotheses to be tested.Theoretical preprint. No model implementation, training, or empirical evaluation is reported. The record contains English and Chinese editions of the same work. candidates.title: Multi-Granularity Distillation of Intervention Sensitivity Representations for Multimodal Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Existing knowledge distillation methods for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) mainly align output distributions or intermediate representations, but rarely supervise how predictions depend on local visual evidence. This limitation may hinder the transfer of fine-grained perception and compositional reasoning. We propose Causal and Multi-source Visual Attribution Distillation (CMVAD), which transfers teacher-derived visual evidence during distillation. Region-level interventions first estimate token-level causal visual attributions, identifying image regions that influence each generated token. The Causal Evidence Adapter Fetch (CEAF) module jointly models token importance and semantic interactions to adaptively aggregate multi-source causal evidence into a unified representation. A Multi-granularity Attribution Distillation (MAD) objective transfers this representation via global evidence distribution alignment, critical-region alignment, and evidence-ranking consistency. Experiments on general visual question answering and compositional reasoning benchmarks show that CMVAD outperforms existing MLLM distillation methods, achieving larger gains in compositional reasoning while retaining competitive visual question answering performance. Results across teacher–student architectures demonstrate its generalizability. We further evaluate VisDrone UAV object detection through overall comparisons, providing supplementary evidence of CMVAD’s applicability to object recognition and localization in UAV imagery.

candidates.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose MAEP (Modality-Aware Expert Pruning), a training-free framework that decomposes expert importance by modality in a single forward pass. MAEP introduces (1) Delta-H Output ($ΔH$), a redistribution-aware metric measuring the MoE output change when an expert is removed, and (2) low-attention vision tokens as a vision-side pruning signal that is dataset-stable: its expert-importance ranking remains stable across different datasets. Text-side importance serves as a preservation signal while vision-side importance serves as a pruning signal, and experts are ranked globally across layers. Experiments on three MoE-based MLLMs across multimodal and text benchmarks show that MAEP outperforms modality-agnostic baselines on the majority of multimodal benchmarks while remaining competitive on text-only tasks, reducing the BF16 expert weight footprint by about 27 GB (about 47% of total memory) so that the full weight footprint of an approximately 58 GB model fits within a single 40 GB GPU. Code is available at https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP.

candidates.title: Graph-Mediated Large Language Model Systems in the Agentic Era: Reasoning, Knowledge, Retrieval, Execution, and Coordination
candidates.abstract: Graphs play an increasingly important role in large language model (LLM) systems, supporting structural reasoning, knowledge grounding, retrieval, and memory. As these systems evolve toward the agentic era, graphs also organize execution dependencies and multi-agent communication, linking intermediate observations and retained information to subsequent decisions. However, understanding their contribution requires distinguishing the function of each graph operation, the component responsible for its computation, and the subsequent use of its output. This survey introduces an operation-level role--locus taxonomy for reasoning, knowledge and evidence, retrieval and memory, execution, and coordination. We compare how graph observations and external computations guide decisions, how memory representations and updates support later tasks, and how dependencies constrain execution and information delivery. These comparisons distinguish improvements in local metrics from downstream task performance while retaining the conditions under which results were reported. We then organize benchmarks, comparison designs, process diagnostics, and system costs into an evaluation framework. Finally, we identify open challenges in adaptive computation and stopping, memory maintenance, and dependency-aware recovery. The survey provides a basis for assessing when graph mechanisms are useful and for evaluating their effects across components and stages.

candidates.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
candidates.abstract: Knowledge editing has become a key technique for updating knowledge in large language models. However, existing methods neglect the geometric structure of the knowledge representation space, leading to two key limitations: they cannot distinguish which pre-trained knowledge should be preferentially preserved (core vs. non-core) nor which new edits are inherently difficult (hard vs. easy). To address this, we propose GEdit, a geometry-aware framework built on a Low-Rank Plus Diagonal (LR+D) factor model that captures the intrinsic low-rank structure of Transformer FFN hidden representations. GEdit features two complementary mechanisms. First, the low-rank regularization applies targeted protection on a low-rank core knowledge subspace. Second, the adaptive regularization dynamically adjusts the regularization strength based on each edit request's editability: relaxing constraints for hard edits to ensure success, and tightening them for easy edits to better preserve pretrained knowledge. Extensive experiments on GPT2-XL, GPT-J, and LLaMA-3-8B under large-scale editing scenarios, including both mini-batch and fully sequential editing settings with up to 10,000 continuous updates, show that GEdit consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both editing success and knowledge preservation.

candidates.title: Commercial multimodal large language models show systematic model-specific errors in breast cancer pathology reporting: a paired concordance study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Breast cancer treatment depends on histopathological features such as Nottingham grade and receptor-defined subtype, yet specialist pathologist access is limited where the workforce is scarce. Commercial multimodal large language models (MLLMs) read hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images through paid interfaces without local hardware, but prior pathology evaluations addressed only coarse tasks. Methods We performed a single-center retrospective paired concordance study comparing three flagship commercial MLLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.5) with a board-certified breast pathologist reference in 427 invasive breast cancers. Each model received the same overview and 16 H&E tissue tiles per case and the same prompt. We assessed item-level concordance for clinically relevant features, compared raw and chance-corrected agreement, and characterized the direction of each model’s errors. In 111 cases, two pathologists blinded to the report re-read the submitted slide, and the image packets given to the models were reviewed separately, to establish slide-level and packet-level references and a within-study interobserver benchmark. Results No model achieved agreement sufficient to support autonomous extraction of any feature. On blinded review of the image packets in 110 cases, lymphovascular invasion was visible in none and perineural invasion in one; Claude and GPT-5.5 reported neither, whereas Gemini reported lymphovascular invasion in 26 packets, none supported by the images. Invasive carcinoma was absent from five packets, for which a Nottingham grade was nevertheless returned in 14 of 15 model-case pairs. Claude ranked highest by raw histological-type concordance (87.4%) yet classified every lobular and micropapillary carcinoma as no-special-type, reversing the ranking in the class-wise sensitivity analysis. In an exploratory negative-control analysis against IHC-defined receptor classes, HER2-positive sensitivity was ≤ 3.6% across all three models, the expected floor for H&E-only input. Two-reader agreement on the submitted slides was moderate (quadratic-weighted kappa for grade, 0.51); model agreement with the report for grade (0.27–0.42) overlapped with that of the second pathologist (0.36). Conclusions None of the three evaluated MLLMs achieved agreement sufficient for autonomous extraction of clinically relevant breast pathology features. Under the same prompt, each model showed a systematic error direction, including positive calls for findings absent from the input; limited secondary analyses in individual models (prompt variants, reasoning-effort, and an alternative higher-tier model from the same vendor) did not eliminate these patterns, and whether they reflect model priors or prompt-model interaction was not resolved. These findings do not support autonomous use; any assistive role would require prospective evaluation with tumor-aware image sampling and pathologist review.

candidates.title: Benchmarking latent-space reasoning abilities in large language models through forced response-language selection
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can perform reasoning computations both internally within their latent space and externally by generating explicit token sequences like chains of thought. Significant progress in enhancing reasoning abilities has been made by scaling test-time compute. However, understanding and quantifying model-internal reasoning abilities – the inferential “leaps” models make between individual token predictions – remains crucial. This study introduces a benchmark (n = 4,000 items) designed to quantify model-internal reasoning in different domains. We achieve this by having LLMs indicate the correct solution to reasoning problems not through descriptive text, but by selecting a specific language of their initial response token that is different from English, the benchmark language. This not only requires models to reason beyond their context window, but at the same time to overcome their default behavior to respond in the same language as the prompt, posing an additional cognitive strain. We evaluate a set of 18 LLMs, showing significant performance variations, with GPT-4.5 achieving the highest accuracy (74.7%), outperforming models like Grok-2 (67.2%), or Llama 3.1 405B (65.6%). Control experiments and difficulty scaling analyses suggest that while LLMs engage in internal reasoning, we cannot rule out heuristic exploitations under certain conditions, marking an area for future investigation. Our experiments demonstrate that LLMs can “think” via latent-space computations, highlighting model-internal inference processes that need further understanding, especially in view of safety-related aspects like covert planning, goal-seeking, or deception emerging without explicit token traces. Significance Statement – Large language models (LLMs) often appear to "reason" only when they show step-by-step chains of thought. We introduce a benchmark that instead measures reasoning carried out silently in a model’s latent space. Tasks require models to infer the correct answer and indicate it solely by choosing a pre-specified non-English response language—preventing them from "thinking in the context window." Across eight reasoning domains, models show wide variation, with some large dense transformer models substantially outperforming others. Control studies and difficulty scaling suggest genuine internal computation, while also revealing potential heuristic shortcuts. By isolating model-internal "reasoning leaps," our approach helps quantify hidden inferences and highlights oversight and safety risks from capabilities that leave no explicit token trace.

candidates.title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery across diverse fields. Yet scientific AI remains constrained by data curation, which demands substantial manual effort and deep domain expertise, creating major cost and scalability barriers. Here we present the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine (AIDE), a multi-agent framework that automates data curation for scientific AI. AIDE collects, selects, and organizes data in three stages, providing an end-to-end pipeline that turns a data request into training-ready datasets. We benchmarked AIDE on 14 tasks across biomedical and chemical domains. Scientific AI models built with AIDE-curated datasets matched or outperformed those built with manually curated data, and AIDE’s fully automated preparation delivered significant gains in efficiency and data utilization without compromising quality. These findings provide consistent evidence of AIDE’s applicability across scientific domains and usage paradigms and demonstrate its potential to accelerate scientific AI development and democratize access to scientific AI. Here, authors develop AIDE, a multiagent framework that automates scientific data curation, and demonstrate across biomedical and chemical tasks that its automatically curated datasets can match or outperform manually curated data while improving efficiency.

candidates.title: BitLLM: Efficient Low-Bit, Conversion-Hiding LLM Decoding on Mobile GPUs
candidates.abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models (LLMs) has unlocked remarkable capabilities across various domains. However, deploying LLMs on mobile devices remains challenging because of their high computational and memory requirements. Low-bit quantization (e.g., 4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) can reduce model size while preserving accuracy, but its practical efficacy on mobile GPUs has been limited so far. In this paper, we identify that the performance gap stems primarily from frequent data type conversions between quantized and floating-point values, and dynamic and inefficient memory access patterns caused by the growing Key-Value (KV) cache during autoregressive decoding. We introduce BitLLM, a mobile inference engine that addresses type conversion overhead and suboptimal memory accesses in quantized LLMs. Our approach features an adaptive layout and packing strategy for the KV cache that ensures efficient memory access throughout LLM decoding. This is coupled with an integer-native execution pipeline that defers and overlaps type conversion outside the compute hot path, keeping the critical MatMul stages in the integer domain. Implemented on off-the-shelf mobile GPUs, BitLLM outperforms leading engines, i.e., LLAMA.CPP, MNN-LLM, LiteRT-LM, and MLC-LLM, achieving average speedups of 1.78×, 1.73×, 1.58×, and 1.47×, respectively, across various models and quantization levels. Under long-context generation, BitLLM reduces average energy consumption (per token) by up to 88.9%.

candidates.title: Software-Defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture for Teleoperation via Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Abstract Precise teleoperation in unstructured environments remains challenging, because human errors and system-inherent limitations such as control jittering can significantly degrade task success and operational efficiency. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a software-defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture (CAVF) system that leverages the open-world understanding of a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The proposed system automatically generates motion guidance for the robot end-effector (EEF) to assist teleoperation, preserving critical task-relevant motion while suppressing unnecessary translation and rotation components. This framework enables the autonomous generation of context-aware, haptic-free assistance without relying on handcrafted rules or physical force-feedback devices. Quantitative experiments in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves success rates, reduces completion times, and enhances trajectory efficiency compared to conventional teleoperation.

candidates.title: Silent methodological failures in AI-assisted science: benchmarking large language model agents for virtual gene knockout analysis
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in computational biology, yet their reliability in executing complex scientific workflows remains poorly characterized. Here, we benchmarked five LLM agents (DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, HY3 Preview, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7) on virtual gene knockout analyses using four computational frameworks across two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. All agents successfully completed the assigned workflows, but their quantitative outputs varied substantially: execution times spanned a 31fold range (61 − 1,920 s), while cross-model coefficients of variation reached 142.1%. Notably, four of five agents (80%) exhibited “silent methodological failures,” generating computationally valid, error-free code that produced biologically implausible results. Among the evaluated agents, GLM 5.1 showed the most balanced performance across computational efficiency and biological plausibility. These findings demonstrate that successful code execution alone does not ensure scientific validity and highlight cross-model concordance and biological validation as important quality-control strategies for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted computational biology workflows.

candidates.title: RAG-X: Systematic Diagnosis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Question Answering
candidates.abstract: Automated question-answering (QA) systems increasingly rely on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground large language models (LLMs) in authoritative medical knowledge, ensuring clinical accuracy and patient safety in AI applications for healthcare. Despite progress in RAG evaluation, current benchmarks focus only on simple multiple-choice QA tasks and employ metrics that poorly capture the semantic precision required for complex QA tasks. These approaches fail to diagnose whether an error stems from faulty retrieval or flawed generation, limiting developers from performing targeted improvement. To address this gap, we propose RAG-X, a diagnostic framework that evaluates the retriever and generator independently across a triad of QA tasks: information extraction, short-answer generation, and multiple-choice question answering. RAG-X introduces Context Utilization Efficiency (CUE) metrics to disaggregate system success into interpretable quadrants, isolating verified grounding from deceptive accuracy. Our experiments reveal an ''Accuracy Fallacy'', where a 14% gap separates perceived system success from evidence-based grounding. By surfacing hidden failure modes, RAG-X offers the diagnostic transparency needed for safe and verifiable clinical RAG systems. Our code is available at https://github.com/AswiniS94/RAG-X_Evaluation.

candidates.title: Retriever as an Attack Surface: Exploring Fairness Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have recently been shown to be vulnerable to fairness and bias manipulation, with prior attacks predominantly targeting the data layer via corpus poisoning. In this work, we expose a fundamentally different and largely unexplored attack surface: the retriever itself. Motivated by the widespread deployment of off-the-shelf neural retrievers as plug-and-play components in modular RAG pipelines, we formalize the Adversarial Fairness Attack against RAG (AFA-RAG), where an adversary manipulates only retriever parameters, leaving both the corpus and generator untouched, to systematically skew evidence exposure toward a target demographic while preserving semantic relevance and stealth. To instantiate this threat, we propose AFA-RL, a reinforcement learning framework that treats the retriever as a strategic ranking agent interacting with a RAG environment. AFA-RL learns adversarial ranking policies that subtly reshape retrieved evidence to bias downstream response generation, guided by a fairness-aware reward with strict relevance and distributional constraints. Experiments across multiple datasets and large language model backbones show that AFA-RL can cause disproportionate fairness degradation with negligible impact on standard retrieval metrics. Our results uncover a previously overlooked supply-chain vulnerability in modular RAG systems and underscore the urgent need for robustness guarantees at the retriever level.

candidates.title: Predicting Partial Answer Quality and Utility in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
candidates.abstract: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a promising paradigm for multi-hop question answering, where a reasoning model iteratively issues queries to a retriever and incorporates newly retrieved context into subsequent reasoning steps. While this iterative process can improve final answer quality, current evaluations of agentic RAG largely focus on end-to-end outcomes and provide limited visibility into how a model's answer state changes during generation. In this work, we introduce an in-trajectory probing framework to study intermediate answer states in agentic RAG. Specifically, after each retrieval-reasoning iteration, we force an agentic model to stop reasoning and generate an intermediate answer based on its current state. This allows us to define two iteration-level measures: partial answer quality at each iteration, and partial utility as the change in partial answer quality across iterations. Our analysis across multi-hop QA benchmarks reveals that partial answer quality often plateaus before natural termination, with many later iterations contributing only small measurable improvements. Accordingly, we formulate two prediction tasks, partial answer quality prediction and partial utility prediction, and study trajectory-derived signals from intra-iteration, inter-iteration, and query-iteration perspectives. Experiments show that partial answer quality is more predictable than partial utility, with supervised models achieving Pearson's r above 0.43 for quality prediction. Finally, using predicted answer quality and utility for early stopping reduces average iteration count by about 11% while preserving about 98% of the final answer quality achieved by natural stopping.

candidates.title: P092 | A PRACTICAL DOMAIN-SPECIFIC RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION FRAMEWORK FOR HEADACHE RESEARCH
candidates.abstract: Background. Headache medicine is characterized by rapidly expanding and heterogeneous scientific literature, particularly on pharmacological treatments. This creates practical difficulties for clinicians and researchers who need rapid, reliable, and source-traceable answers to focused and detailed scientific questions. Although large language models can support biomedical summary, their unguided use is limited by the risk of inaccurate, outdated, or non-verifiable statements. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers a practical solution by linking generative models to a selected, personalized and controlled scientific corpus. Herein we describe the development and practical use of a domain-specific RAG system designed to support headache research.Methods. A personalized RAG workflow was developed using a local library of headache-related studies selected and controlled by the researcher. Documents were ingested through a Python-based pipeline that extracted full text and metadata, corrected or integrated bibliographic information when available, removed duplicates, and organized the corpus into structured libraries with searchable metadata.Full texts were divided into overlapping chunks, embedded using OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, and stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with pgvector indexing. Rule-based topic classification enabled optional category-restricted retrieval. A FastAPI backend exposed retrieval, health, and version endpoints and was deployed through Render.com, while GitHub was used for version control and reproducible deployment. Customized GPT agents were connected to the retrieval API through an OpenAPI schema and instructed to retrieve evidence from the indexed corpus before generating answers. This architecture was designed to keep clinicians and researchers in full control of the documents, metadata, and information sources used by the system.Results. The system provided a low-cost, modular, and traceable environment for querying selected headache literature eliminating the so-called hallucinations. In practical use, users can ask focused questions on mechanisms, diagnostic criteria, pharmacological treatments, or methodological issues. The agent retrieves relevant passages from the organized, personal library, summarizes the evidence, reports methodological details when available, and links outputs to local source material. This supports rapid preliminary evidence mapping, paper identification, and hypothesis generation.Conclusions. A personalized, domain-specific RAG system may provide a practical tool for literature-grounded scientific work in headache medicine. Its main value is not to replace systematic reviews or expert interpretation, but to accelerate targeted retrieval, improve traceability, organize scientific libraries, and reduce unsupported generation. An important direction of ongoing development is the transition toward fully local and free/open-source RAG systems.

candidates.title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Post-training updates change what large language models (LLMs) can answer, but may leave their answerability judgments misaligned. We study this knowledge-judgment desynchronization through functional feeling of knowing (FoK), which supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing without implying subjective experience. We propose two trainable channels: a knowledge channel that changes answerability and a FoK channel that judges the current knowledge state. Three stages train them: on-policy supervised fine-tuning (OP-SFT) updates knowledge from corrected on-policy answers; knowledge-delta FoK training (K$Δ$-FT) adapts judgments across intermediate knowledge states; and FoK-guided policy optimization (FGPO) trains the subsequent answer or explanation. Factual-QA experiments, cross-dataset evaluation, and three sequential updates show that explicit FoK alignment improves judgment quality on updated knowledge. MMLU and ARC-Easy separately assess capability preservation.

candidates.title: A Tutorial on Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLM-based Recommender Systems
candidates.abstract: Recommender systems are essential to real-world online services due to their substantial business value. Increasingly, large language models (LLMs) have been adopted for recommendation tasks, owing to their strong reasoning capabilities and their effectiveness in handling cold-start items. A large body of work has sought to adapt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for LLM-based recommender systems by retrieving information from external databases and integrating it into the LLM's input to improve recommendation quality. Despite the rapid growth of the field, existing tutorials lack a clear taxonomy and a dedicated review of RAG methods for LLM-based recommender systems. To fill this gap, we present the first tutorial on this topic. First, we discuss the types of information used in LLM-based recommender systems, including target-user information and external databases for retrieval. Second, we present the design space of RAG for LLM-based recommender systems, outlining the key design choices at each stage of the pipeline: (1) retrieval, (2) augmentation, and (3) generation. Lastly, we introduce open questions for future research on this topic.

candidates.title: persian-rag: A Persian-First Retrieval-Augmented Generation Toolkit — Normalization, Hybrid Retrieval, and Retrieval Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems processing Persian text encounter reduced retrieval accuracy due to character orthography variants, inconsistent Zero-Width Non-Joiner (ZWNJ) usage, mixed numeric representations, non-standardized punctuation, spelling variations, and word reversal during PDF text extraction. This report describes persian-rag (version 0.4.0), an open-source Python library designed to address these language-specific processing stages. The package provides configurable Persian text normalization, document loaders with main-content web extraction and PDF visual-order repair, chunking, dense and sparse retrieval with Persian spelling-variant query expansion, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), cross-encoder and LLM reranking, citation tracking, and a FastAPI HTTP server. On a 34-passage, 42-question benchmark (persian-rag-bench), sparse BM25 Hit@1 increases from 0.881 to 0.952 with spelling-variant query expansion. Dense retrieval with the default model intfloat/multilingual-e5-small and E5 prefixes reaches 0.9881 nDCG@10 on persian-rag-bench, 0.7461 nDCG@10 on a pooled MIRACL Persian dev subset, and 0.9242 nDCG@10 on PQuAD validation. Primary limitations include small benchmark sizes, near-saturated scores, an open issue in query-variant weighting, and the absence of quantitative evaluations for reranking, citation accuracy, and PDF text repair. This is a technical report and has not been peer-reviewed.

candidates.title: Performance-Adaptive Instruction-Template Assignment for Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Instruction-tuning corpora are commonly constructed by pairing fixed input--output examples with static or randomly sampled instruction templates. However, for clinical reasoning, different candidate instruction templates may emphasize different learning signals, including diagnostic conclusion, evidence synthesis, and explanation structure. This paper studies instruction-template assignment as a training-time corpus-construction problem: given fixed clinical input--output examples and a pool of candidate templates, can performance feedback guide template assignment during fine-tuning? This paper presents Performance-Adaptive Instruction-Template Assignment (PAITA), a framework that uses validation feedback to assign instruction templates to fixed clinical input--output examples during fine-tuning. Unlike static assignment, which repeatedly applies one template, or random assignment, which samples templates without regard to observed performance, PAITA balances exploration of alternative templates with exploitation of templates associated with stronger validation feedback. We evaluate PAITA primarily using LLaMA-3-8B and further examine instruction-template assignment across additional model settings using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and BioMedLM-2.7B on the Clinical Reasoning task; Clinical Diagnosis and Medical QA serve as auxiliary evaluations. PAITA improves clinical reasoning conclusion accuracy over static assignment (0.397 vs. 0.372; +2.5 percentage points, p=0.001) and random template assignment (0.397 vs. 0.383; +1.4 percentage points, p=0.044), with additional gains in several reasoning-quality metrics. Auxiliary results and template-assignment analyses further suggest that performance-adaptive assignment can provide benefits beyond instruction diversity alone. These findings support instruction-template assignment as an important design variable in supervised instruction tuning of clinical LLMs.

candidates.title: LSH-KV: Efficient KV Cache Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference via Locality-Sensitive Hashing
candidates.abstract: As large language models increasingly support long-context inference, the computation and memory access overhead of attention and KV caches have become critical bottlenecks for inference latency and system scalability. Existing approaches mitigate these costs through KV cache dropping, approximate attention, or system-level optimizations, but often incur non-trivial trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and implementation complexity. In this work, we propose LSH-KV, a coarse-to-fine KV retrieval framework for efficient long-context LLM inference. LSH-KV uses locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) as a lightweight, training-free coarse partitioning layer for similarity-preserving organization of global KV entries. Within each hash bucket, LSH-KV further uses product quantization with offline-precomputed codebooks for efficient approximate similarity estimation, followed by exact re-ranking to preserve attention accuracy. To further improve system efficiency, LSH-KV introduces a score-aware block-level cache management strategy that aligns KV movement between CPU and GPU with retrieval relevance. Experimental results on long-context benchmarks demonstrate that LSH-KV significantly reduces end-to-end inference latency while preserving generation quality, even when selective attention is performed using only a fraction of the input tokens. These results show that LSH-KV enables scalable, robust, and accurate inference under long-context settings. The code is available at https://github.com/HarryFunn/lsh-kv.

candidates.title: LEDGER: A Long-Context Benchmark of Corporate Annual Reports for Grounded Financial Retrieval and Extraction
candidates.abstract: Finance reporting is a natural proving ground for large language models, and the very-long-context capabilities of recent models across all sizes make rigorous evaluation in this domain an increasingly pressing need. Yet most public financial resources reduce the task to plain-text SEC 10-K filings paired with a handful of question--answer items. We release Ledger (Long-context Evaluation of Documents for Grounded Extraction and Retrieval), a corpus of 4, 999 digitized corporate annual reports --- full documents with figures, tables, and narrative, not just regulatory filings. Each report is labeled with 31 consolidated financial KPIs to be extracted and linked to the market's reaction at the earnings date. From this data we derive three evaluation benchmarks spanning the difficulty spectrum: a pure page-level KPI retrieval task with TREC-style relevance judgments over 118,048 questions in natural language, a conversational ''needle-in-a-haystack'' single-value lookup, and a full KPI extraction task, both from long, numerically dense reports. We additionally provide human OCR-quality annotations with inter-annotator agreement and the complete extraction, validation, and scoring toolchain. We further demonstrate the dataset's research utility with a case study linking CEO-letter rhetoric to post-publication market impact. An extension to 291 French ESEF filers (1, 153 reports with 24 KPIs) augments the corpus.

candidates.title: Trusting Imagined Futures: Auditing Imagined Rewards for VLA Post-Training
candidates.abstract: Video world models enable candidate actions to be evaluated through imagined outcomes, but high predicted rewards can favor trajectories with poor execution quality. We introduce Trusting Imagined Futures (TIF), an offline supervision selection method for vision-language-action (VLA) post-training that audits predicted rewards using execution feedback. A multidimensional reward model predicts a utility score for candidate ranking and five dimensions of execution quality. An auditor uses reward predictions and uncertainty to identify overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined videos and real executions. TIF accepts the candidate with the highest predicted utility when its advantage over the existing trajectory exceeds a margin and its audit risk passes a threshold; otherwise, it retains the existing supervision. The retained real trajectories then supervise behavior cloning. Across four LIBERO suites and three training seeds, TIF achieves a mean success rate of 76.25%, improving over training on the existing trajectories by 3.00 percentage points with the same trajectory count and training budget. Adding audit gating yields 1.47 percentage points with the reward model and advantage margin held fixed. The gains persist against advantage ranking and logistic regression risk selection at matched replacement counts. On recorded videos from three real robot tasks, TIF increases clean completion among selected trajectories from 58.33% to 70.00% across 60 candidate pools.

candidates.title: The Novelty Horizon H_N: Why Large Language Models Fail to Generate Scientific Data beyond Their Training Distribution
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) lack physical grounding and extrapolation. This paper formalises the Novelty Horizon as tasks needing extrapolation beyond training support, causal reasoning absent from learned correlations, or post-frontier information. A forensic analysis tests LLMs on unguided, guided, and ground-truth data from an underrepresented diode-clamped short-circuit experiment using temporal, spectral, and statistical validation against a first-principles Modified Ohm's Law. Both script-based approaches fail catastrophically with physical and spectral inconsistencies, extreme statistical pathologies, zero Generative Fidelity Score, and linear-regime outputs. Direct prompting corroborates distinct failure modes. This paper introduces the Past Information Boundary and physics-based authentication. LLM data generation cannot extrapolate past the Novelty Horizon essential for novel discovery. Hybrid neuro-symbolic systems must preserve human causal reasoning and experimental design.

candidates.title: RAFT: Reasoning-Aligned Fine-Tuning Improves Robustness of VLA Post-Training
candidates.abstract: Adapting a generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a target task with limited demonstrations can improve nominal task success while reducing robustness to variations in appearance, objects, and instructions. We introduce reasoning-aligned fine-tuning (RAFT), a two-stage post-training procedure: RAFT first trains low-rank adapters on task-relevant reasoning annotations, then freezes them while fine-tuning the policy on action demonstrations. On a physical DROID robot, RAFT achieves $75.0\%$ out-of-distribution success, compared with $27.9\%$ for plain fine-tuning; on a multi-stage bimanual YAM task, it reaches $70.0\%$ mean success, compared with $36.0\%$ for the strongest baseline. RAFT also improves success under visual, object, and instruction shifts in simulated pick-and-place and open-drawer tasks. Compared with plain fine-tuning, RAFT policies place more attention on annotated task regions and yield higher linear-probe accuracy for object identity in later layers. A broader reasoning-data mixture further improves downstream success across demonstration budgets.

candidates.title: Precision Transition Dynamics: Standardizing BF16 to U8 Containers in Sub-Block Quantization for Edge LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: Journal Description Title: Precision Transition Dynamics: Standardizing BF16 to U8 Containers in Sub-Block Quantization for Edge LLM Inference Author: Andri Johandri (Independent AI Research Team, POKDARTIK, Pemalang, Indonesia / WiTi4Bit Project) Main Topic: Post-training quantization (PTQ) and memory container standardization for efficient Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained edge hardware. Core Contributions & Highlights: Precision Transition Dynamics (PTD) Framework: The paper introduces a deterministic, bit-level sub-block quantization framework that operates without requiring external calibration data. PTD leverages canonical binary routing for exponents and structured mapping of mantissas via mirror pairs combined with a strict round-half-up mechanism to eliminate stochastic rounding noise. Hybrid U8 Safetensors Container Architecture: It proposes a 1,000,000-element threshold to safeguard architectural stability. Sensitive layers (such as layer normalization and key-value projections) are isolated in split-FP16 format, while massive weight tensors are compressed into compact QnM blocks (18 bytes per 32-element sub-block). Empirical Evaluation Results: Evaluated on the Gemma-3-1B-IT architecture, the Q4M implementation achieved a 70.8% size reduction (3.42x compression ratio), shrinking model weights from 2.00 GB to 584.8 MB. Furthermore, the model maintained high logit fidelity with an average cosine similarity of 0.9556 alongside robust text generation capabilities. Resources & Repositories: Quantized Model Repository: Hugging Face - gemma-3-1b-it-qnm-4bit Inference Runtime Toolchain: GitHub - runtime_chat

candidates.title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
candidates.abstract: Abstract Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

candidates.title: Memory-Constrained Inference for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: This technical white paper investigates the feasibility and performance constraints of running large language models on memory-constrained consumer hardware, with particular emphasis on sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures, expert placement, storage bandwidth, and local code-generation workloads. Three specialized inference systems, Colibri, Flash-MoE, and Strata, are examined in terms of their approaches to distributing model weights across GPU memory, system RAM, and persistent storage. Published implementation details and performance measurements are analyzed, including the effects of expert caching, routing configurations, memory residency, and storage I/O. An analytical hardware comparison evaluates three computing configurations: an Apple M5 MacBook Pro with 16 GB unified memory, an NVIDIA RTX 3060 laptop with 6 GB VRAM and 16 GB system RAM, and a reference RTX 4060 Ti desktop with 16 GB VRAM and 32 GB system RAM. Model-memory requirements, context-length sensitivity, and accelerator-memory limitations are examined under consistent assumptions. For code-generation applications, the paper proposes evaluating inference systems using elapsed time per successfully accepted code patch rather than relying exclusively on tokens-per-second measurements. A reproducible benchmarking methodology is outlined to support future comparisons of inference performance, memory utilization, storage traffic, and coding-task success. The analysis identifies Colibri as a primary experimental candidate for larger MoE deployments on the examined NVIDIA systems, while retaining conventional inference engines such as llama.cpp and MLX LM as comparison baselines where appropriate. The work distinguishes published benchmarks, analytical estimates, and locally recorded measurements from proposed experiments. It does not claim a completed head-to-head evaluation of the three specialized inference systems.

candidates.title: MADClean: Statistical Profiling and Multi-Agent Large Language Model Reasoning for Automatic Data Cleaning
candidates.abstract: High-quality data is essential for effective decision-making, data analytics, and training machine learning models. Numerous data cleaning tools and systems have been proposed in both academia and industry. Several recent tools utilize Large Language Models (LLMs), but most rely entirely on their unverified reasoning capabilities, struggling to effectively handle dirty datasets with heterogeneous error types. In this demo, we describe MADClean, a tabular data cleaning system that uses statistical profiling and a multi-agent architecture to achieve strong performance in several data cleaning tasks. MADClean uses dedicated LLM agents to recommend cleaning operations, generate executable source code, and iteratively verify and improve its outputs. We show that MADClean reliably handles dirty data across three real-world data cleaning scenarios, and scales to datasets with hundreds of thousands of rows in our evaluation.

candidates.title: Large Language Models in Fruit Science
candidates.abstract: This chapter reviews large language models (LLMs) applications and future prospects in fruit sciences. LLMs are advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on extensive datasets, and are revolutionizing how fruit scientists and agriculturists interact with and analyze data. Analysis of genetic data, interpretation of climate data, and forecasting of market trends are some of the topics that are covered. These models make it easier to automate the annotation of data, improve decision support systems for precision agriculture, and reveal client preferences and market behaviors for forecasting. In addition, the ethical implications and difficulties that are linked with the deployment of LLMs are elaborated. Case studies from the real world, such as AI-powered pest monitoring and irrigation systems, are presented to illustrate the practical advantages of LLMs in terms of increasing yield, lowering resource use, and improving the overall efficiency of fruit production. LLMs will be integrated into fruit science in the future, but more research and collaboration are needed to maximize their potential in this dynamic sector.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Forecasting of Electricity Price Spikes
candidates.abstract: Can market notices read by a large language model (LLM) improve short-horizon electricity price spike forecasts? We study five regions of Australia's National Electricity Market. A local LLM extracted features once per notice, only notices visible at the forecast origin were used, and a gradient-boosting model produced onset probabilities. In an out-of-sample development back-test (July 2022 to July 2024), notice features did not lower the 60-minute Brier score of a numeric model including the market operator's next-hour forecasts. At 24 hours they did, but rule-based features did so almost equally and attribution to notice content was not established. A locally frozen protocol, not publicly deposited, governed a retrospective single-use holdout from 15 August to 17 October 2026. At 60 minutes, the hypothesis that LLM features lower the numeric model's Brier score was not established (H1; relative Brier skill -0.09%), so the planned comparison with rule-based features was not tested (H2). At 24 hours, the hypothesis that LLM features lower the score against a text-free control was not established (H3; +0.37%, 95% CI [-9.74, 1.39], inconclusive). By the frozen wording rule the non-significant 24-hour improvement comes mainly from recalibration and cannot be attributed to notice content, although post hoc the decomposition could not separate recalibration from resolution. The 24-hour base rate was 1.56% on the holdout against 14.0% in development. With 5 onsets on 3 days and 24-hour positives in 2 of 22 three-day blocks, the holdout neither established nor excluded a 24-hour effect.

candidates.title: Large Language Model as Universal Retriever in Industrial-Scale Recommender System
candidates.abstract: In real-world recommender systems, different retrieval objectives are typically addressed using task-specific datasets with carefully designed model architectures. We demonstrate that Large Language Models (LLMs) can function as universal retrievers, capable of handling multiple objectives within a generative retrieval framework. To address the model expressiveness and inference efficiency issues of generative retrieval, we propose multi-query representation and transferable discriminative mapping layers to model complex user-item relationships, and incorporate probabilistic sampling to reduce computation costs. Finally, our Universal Retrieval Model (URM) can adaptively generate a set from tens of millions of candidates based on an arbitrary given objective while keeping the latency within tens of milliseconds. Applied to industrial-scale data, URM outperforms expert models elaborately designed for different retrieval objectives in offline experiments and achieves a 3.13% revenue increase on our online advertising platform. URM also demonstrates strong performance in impression and GMV for long-tail and cold-start items.

candidates.title: Large Language Model Use in Agronomy
candidates.abstract: This study explores how large language models (LLMs) can transform agronomic research and precision agriculture. As the fourth paradigm in agriculture, following mechanization, chemical usage, and genetic interventions, LLMs are poised to revolutionize farming practices. In soil and crop management, LLMs offer context-specific advice for tasks such as weed control, nutrient management, irrigation scheduling, plant scouting, and disease diagnosis, leading to improved resource efficiency, higher crop yields, and enhanced environmental sustainability. The study also highlights LLMs’ promise in tracking crop health and estimating yield. By leveraging hyperspectral imaging and deep learning techniques, LLMs can accurately assess crop stress, disease, and growth stages. For yield prediction, combining LLMs with biophysical crop models and multidimensional data offers a sophisticated approach to understand complex crop–environment interactions. Furthermore, LLMs are being adopted in various agricultural domains, including smart livestock farming, precision aquaculture, and agricultural extension services. They offer personalized advice to farmers, interpret satellite imagery, and even assist in coding and experimental design. However, challenges persist in data quality, privacy, scalability, and ethical concerns. The research underscores the need for collaborative efforts between agronomists, digital designers, and other stakeholders to 178 fully realize LLMs’ potential. It suggests that by integrating LLMs with traditional wisdom and improving data management, agronomists can pioneer a new paradigm in their field. As LLMs mature, they exhibit the promise of significantly enhancing agronomic skills, driving sustainable farming practices, and ultimately contributing to global food security.

candidates.title: Insect Study Through Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs), a type of artificial intelligence, mimic human language patterns, enabling comprehension, prediction, and generation of valuable content. In agricultural entomology—the study of insects—LLMs like ChatGPT offer transformative potential for education and research. They simplify complex topics such as insect ecology, life stages, integrated pest management, and species identification, making them accessible for teaching and learning. LLMs assist educators by reducing workload in curriculum design, grading, and developing engaging teaching strategies for practical activities. These technologies enhance knowledge sharing, scientific writing, and research in insect–plant interactions. This chapter explores the role of LLMs in advancing pedagogy, improving insect and pest identification, and addressing ethical concerns and challenges with their application in entomology. By leveraging LLMs, educators and researchers can revolutionize approaches to agricultural entomology, enriching both teaching and scientific exploration.

candidates.title: Filter-then-match: Holistic Schema Matching via Small Language Model Filtering and Large Language Model Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Schema matching (SM) is a critical step in data integration pipelines and serves as a foundation for tasks such as Table Search and Entity Matching. However, applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to SM is prohibitively expensive due to the task's inherent quadratic complexity, which hinders scalable and cost-efficient deployment. In this paper, we investigate two SM scenarios: the most common instance-based scenario where headers and their values are available, and the metadata-based scenario where only metadata is provided (e.g., due to privacy constraints). We propose Fermat, a unified framework designed to address both scenarios effectively. Fermat incorporates a Small Language Model (SLM)-based filtering strategy that significantly reduce the computational overhead of applying LLMs to SM. We also introduce a column synthesis workflow that enables a fully unsupervised solution, effectively mitigating the scarcity of ground-truth data. Additionally, we implement a specialized loss function with hard column mining to counteract the biases of the filter model on imbalanced data, ensuring improved recall of positive candidates. Finally, we conduct comprehensive reproduction and evaluation of recent schema matching methods on both metadata-based and instance-based datasets, providing insights into their generalizability across diverse scenarios.

candidates.title: Evolution of Large Language Models and Agricultural Sciences
candidates.abstract: Imagine a world where humans and computers converse as rapidly as friends. OpenAI’s Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) models are creating this future by giving gadgets human-like conversational skills. GPT-4 and other GPT models represent some of the newest advances in artificial intelligence (AI). These are large language models (LLMs) that are trained using extensive datasets to understand and generate text that creates human-like text with great precision. These AI models will have effects that go beyond voice assistants. With OpenAI’s models, developers can now use natural language processing to make apps that decode human wants in ways that were existing in science fiction. One can use GPT-4 and 4 ChatGPT ideas in everything from research paper writing ideas, tools for learning that are tailored to each student. Yet, what do GPT-4 and ChatGPT mean? This chapter introduces the fundamentals, genesis, and key attributes of LLMs and their emerging applications in agricultural sciences.

candidates.title: Cite Unseen: Measuring Citation-Channel Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
candidates.abstract: Citation-grounded retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems expose source URLs alongside answers, extending user trust to cited links. Prior corpus-poisoning research primarily targets answer corruption, overlooking cases where answers remain largely unchanged while citations route users to unsafe destinations. We identify this citation-channel vulnerability and introduce Citation-stage Attack Success Rate (C-ASR) to separate citation manipulation from answer degradation. Across four BEIR corpora, three retrievers, and four generators, changing only the source URL of a single injected document reaches 71% C-ASR on the most vulnerable generator at well under 1% corpus pollution. The attack persists with paraphrased or answer-derived content, while citation behavior differs sharply across generators under our fixed pipeline. These results expose a model-dependent safety surface missed by answer-centric RAG evaluation.

candidates.title: Can Large Language Models Engineer Parallel Workflows?
candidates.abstract: Scientific workflows are specified using specialized languages to define parallel execution, an expertise that domain users may lack. Large Language Models (LLMs) can lower this barrier, but existing evaluations stop at syntactic analysis and do not verify whether the generated specifications execute or preserve parallelism. In this paper, we evaluated four LLMs in two workflow engineering tasks (workflow specification from natural-language and conversion across workflow systems), covering three workflow systems, three workflows, and two prompting strategies. For each generated workflow specification, we analyzed its executability and whether it executes in parallel. Results show that lexical similarity to expert-developed workflows is a poor predictor of executability, that in-context examples improve execution rates unevenly across systems, and that several workflow specifications collapse into serial execution. Even those that support parallelism are consistently slower than the expert-developed workflow.

candidates.title: Application of Large Language Models in Agricultural Entomology
candidates.abstract: Agricultural entomology, a critical field focused on the study of insects that affect crop production, benefits greatly from advances in artificial intelligence (AI), by using large language models (LLMs) such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4. These models, trained on large datasets, demonstrate remarkable natural language understanding and solution generation capabilities that can be used to address a variety of agricultural entomology challenges. LLMs make it easier to analyze large amounts of entomological literature, allowing researchers to quickly access and synthesize data on insect behavior, pest management strategies, and the ecological impacts of various species. LLMs can also help develop intelligent advisory systems that provide farmers with real-time, data-driven pest control recommendations, thereby improving sustainable agricultural practices. The use of LLMs in predictive modeling improves forecasting pest outbreaks by analyzing climate and environmental data. This chapter investigates the potential applications of LLMs in agricultural entomology, emphasizing their ability to accelerate research, improve decision-making processes, and promote precision agriculture. The discussion will include case studies of successful implementations, challenges in integrating AI with traditional entomological research, and future directions for using LLMs to advanced field. These advanced 94 technologies offer significant advantages in agricultural entomology; their application also presents several drawbacks, which can be balanced by joint approaches that integrate LLMs with human expertise, improve data quality, ensure transparency, and build the necessary infrastructure to support the use of advanced AI in agricultural entomology.

candidates.title: AdSteer: Native Advertising in Large Language Model Generation
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) services face rapidly rising serving costs. To sustain free or affordable access for a broad user base, alternative monetization mechanisms are needed. Native advertising offers a promising approach, as it creates economic value by aligning user intent with merchant offerings. Yet how to integrate sponsored content naturally into LLM responses remains largely underexplored. Existing approaches primarily rely on prompt-level injection, multi-pass rewriting, or fine-tuning, which can compromise response quality or introduce additional computational costs. We propose AdSteer, a lightweight decoding-time advertising framework that adaptively adjusts token probabilities to integrate contextually appropriate advertisement into responses. AdSteer calibrates the strength and duration of advertising influence, making sponsored content a natural part of the response. Experiments on GEM-Bench across three application scenarios show that AdSteer achieves an average improvement of 14.1% in overall score over the strongest baselines and 22.5% fewer total tokens on average than rewrite-based methods. These results demonstrate that AdSteer provides an effective and practical solution for native advertising in LLMs.
